detail: Proof sites for the one-record identity and each sub-record placement, all read at the pre-conversion revision. BASE IDENTITY: line 1794 `if (!(u8)fn_800DACD8((s32)movie, header))` proves fn_800DACD8's param_1 is the same pointer fn_800DA920 calls `movie`; line 1456 `gMovieStreamState = movie = (u8*)__construct_new_array(movie, fn_800DB0F8, fn_800DB008, 464, 1)` proves the global and the local are one object and fixes the size at 464 = 0x1D0; fn_800DA60C's self+400/+368/+336/+32/+28 (lines 1618-1633) are numerically identical to movie+0x190/0x170/0x150/0x20/0x1C. SIZE: AllocHiMem(472) at line 1455 = 464 + the 8-byte new[] cookie, corroborating the 464 element size. STREAM at 0x20: already cast as `(MovieChunkStream*)(movie + 0x20)` at lines 1656/1693/1695/1696/1713 and `(MovieChunkStream*)(gMovieStreamState + 0x20)` at 1672; line 1855 `*(u32*)(movie + 80) = *(u32*)(movie + 212)` is stream.videoFrameLimit (0x20+0x30) <- videoStreamHeader+0x20. OUTFORMAT at 0x7C: line 1823 passes `movie + 124` as fn_800D99AC's `dst`, whose body (lines 1129-1137) reads dst+4/dst+8 as width/height and writes dst+14 (u16 bitCount), dst+16 (compression), dst+20 (sizeImage); fn_800DA920 then overwrites those same displacements at lines 1824-1828 with bitCount=16 (movie+138=0x8A), compression=3 (movie+140=0x8C) and masks 0xF800/2016/31 at movie+164/168/172 = 0xA4/0xA8/0xAC -- BI_BITFIELDS RGB565, which only makes sense at a BITMAPINFOHEADER's +0x28/+0x2C/+0x30. FILEFORMAT at 0x194: lines 1906-1919 write all 14 fields from the .avi 'strf' chunk in order, with ReadU16LE at exactly param_1+0x1A0 and +0x1A2 -- i.e. +0x0C/+0x0E into the record, the BITMAPINFOHEADER planes/bitCount pair -- and the cast widths in the source (u16 there, u32 everywhere else) independently confirm the field widths. DECODECALL at 0x11C: lines 1832-1833 wire `*(u8**)(movie + 288) = movie + 404` and `*(u8**)(movie + 296) = movie + 124`, i.e. decodeCall.context (0x120) <- &fileFormat (0x194) and decodeCall.bitmap (0x128) <- &outFormat (0x7C), matching the already-accepted MovieDecodeCall typedef field-for-field; line 1711 `decode(movie + 0x150, movie + 0x11C, 0)` and line 1835 MovieValidateFrameFormat(movie+336, movie+284) pass 0x11C as that record. DECODER at 0x150 and its vtable at 0x170: fn_800DB008 tears it down as `fn_800DBD30((MovieDTextOuter*)(self + 0x54), -1)` on a u32* self (0x54 words = 0x150), and fn_800DBE04 sets the vtable with `p[8] = lbl_801296CC` (+0x20), so 0x150+0x20 = 0x170 -- exactly the word fn_800DA60C line 1628 calls close() through and fn_800DA6A4 line 1710 fetches decode() from. STREAM HEADERS at 0xB4/0xE8: lines 1887-1900 and 1924-1937 are two structurally identical 0x34-byte offset-preserving copies; line 1799 computes frameRate as `movie+204 / movie+200` = videoStreamHeader+0x18 / +0x14, the AVI dwRate/dwScale pair. NEGATIVE RESULT recorded deliberately: `gdlmem.py struct` returns no PDB type for Movie, MoviePlayer, VQMovie, AviStream, AVIStream, MovieStream or CMovie, and research/xbox_symbols/functions_by_module.txt shows the Xbox MOVIE.OBJ exports InitMovie/ServeMovie/KillMovie/PlayMovie -- an unrelated cutscene subsystem -- so the absence of PDB authority is a true absence, not a name miss. MACHINE CHECK: a standalone host-gcc replica of MovieState and its five embedded types asserted 34 sizeof/offsetof values against the displacements above and reported ALL OK with sizeof(MovieState) == 0x1D0, matching __construct_new_array's 464 exactly; the same check caught a real error first pass (MovieDTextOuter's declared extent is 0x30, not the 0x34 its comment implies), which is why MovieState keeps that region as opaque words instead of embedding the type.
